question.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254142/assets/1714eb4797f7b318f5e957db7ab0f322fffb2eb2c9bf03f68e3acc08ec399849.svg)

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
question.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $x \geq 0,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254142/assets/4f0d336b322f68550c50d65380e26ffb33bdd55beab0c7d429e7b4055f973b57.svg)

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{0}^{x}{e}^{-t}\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & =-{e}^{-t}{|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-{e}^{-x}+1 \\  & =1-{e}^{-x}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14254142/assets/9e1b63a37177781672b70c3a6c01b1b752164b976b6e9982e07d510d468353aa.svg)
